notes: Focused public-API evidence for IEEE 1516.2-2025 clause 6.2.8 and the IEEE 1516.1-2025 Table 21 standardized-time-representation requirement (Requirements Lab maps that statement only to clause 8). The valid C++ scenario now creates schema-valid FDDs selecting both HLAinteger64Time and HLAfloat64Time, checks each joined factory name, initial/final/zero/epsilon values, epsilon advancement, interval difference, and logical-time/interval encoding round trips. Rejection cases continue to cover raw basic and reference types as InconsistentFOM and valid federation-name reuse. The catalog's added clause-8 relationship is focused support evidence, not exhaustive Table 21 or conformance validation. Existing Java parity runs cover only the prior integer64 acceptance behavior and rejection cases; Java float64 acceptance has not been added. Other Java providers, private composition APIs, diagnostic-text, interoperability, and conformance are not claimed.
